summary: Redwood AE + SE walked the Vantage Retail team through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for a customer-facing chat+recommendations system with strong latency needs and strict PCI-like controls. Key asks: per-route cost modelling, multi-tenant cost allocation, SOC2/KMS compliance, and a short benchmarking POC.
topics: Batching & caching impact on unit economics
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-12 15:00 PDT / Duration 42m
Attendees: Ethan Park, Sofia Ramirez (Redwood); Maya Chen, Oliver Grant, Priya Nair (Vantage Retail)

[00:00] Ethan: All right, hey everyone thanks for joining, um this is Ethan from Redwood, and Sofia will walk through the console, we said 40 minutes so we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:32] Maya: Great thanks, we've been looking forward to seeing the per-route stuff, thanks for doing this.
[00:45] Sofia: Cool, I'll share my screen now. Let me know if the deck or the console comes up.
[01:05] Sofia: (screen share) So first slide is quick context - Console -> usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. We'll start with the overall usage view, then zoom into a per-route breakdown for your chat endpoint and the recommendations endpoint, and then show cost allocation and what impacts unit economics.
[01:26] Oliver: Sounds good, our main thing is predictable cost, and also isolating costs by product route for chargeback.
[01:40] Sofia: Totally. Jumping into the Console - Overview tab. You can see top-level token volume, request rates, p50/p95 latency, error rate. There's a tokens-over-time chart and then a per-model usage table.
[02:10] Sofia: Quick note - model variants are auto-detected and we show quantized vs full precision usage separately. You can filter by model, region, and deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated).
[02:35] Priya: On the quantization note - do you show which requests hit quantized kernels vs non-quantized? We have a mix in production.
[02:45] Sofia: Yes - on the per-route view we break down by model variant and quantization profile. It's a tag on the request so you can group and see cost delta.
[03:05] Ethan: Important to note, quantization saved customers we've seen 20-40% cost per token but can have small perf variance depending on sequence length.
[03:20] Maya: Cool. Show us a per-route dashboard for chat please.
[03:30] Sofia: Opening route: /chat-v2. Here we have a timeline of requests, average tokens per request, batching effectiveness, and a cost-per-request metric. There's a stacked bar for model variants and a second panel with token-level cost breakdown (compute vs infra).
[04:05] Sofia: The compute estimate is derived from GPU-second consumption normalized by model profile; infra includes networking, storage for KV cache, etc. We let you toggle to include or exclude caching credit.
[04:25] Oliver: How accurate is that compute estimate? We need something we can plug into our finance model.
[04:35] Sofia: It's calibrated based on our serving runtime telemetry and can be adjusted with your actual GPU pricing if you choose Dedicated or for custom cost modeling. For Hosted we provide an estimated unit cost which maps to the pricing tiers.
[05:00] Priya: If we go Dedicated, can we get raw metrics (GPU utilization, kernel-level timings) to reconcile?
[05:10] Sofia: Yep, Dedicated exposes more detailed telemetry in the console and via the metrics API. We can also provide CSV exports with per-request breakdown for the POC.
[05:28] Ethan: Also worth calling out automatic prefix/KV caching - you can see cache hit rates by route which drastically affects effective cost per request.
[05:45] Maya: Show the caching panel.
[05:50] Sofia: Here's the caching panel - hit rate, average KV size, and estimated token savings. In this example route we see 35% prefix cache hit and 18% KV reuse, which reduced token generation by about 22%.
[06:20] Maya: Nice. That helps with cost.
[06:25] Sofia: Next, batching. We surface batching efficiency - average batch size, waiting latency, and whether it's continuous batching or single-request. You can set batch target windows in Optimize and see simulated cost/latency tradeoffs.
[06:45] Oliver: So we can intentionally increase batching to save cost but we'll trade latency - can you show a simulation?
[06:53] Sofia: Sure - switching to the Optimize tab. There's a knob: target batch size vs p95 latency. If we move the slider to increase batch size from 1.2 to 3.5 requests, estimated unit cost drops ~28% but p95 goes up ~40ms in this profile.
[07:20] Sofia: We provide recommended quantization profiles per route too, so the console will say "Recommend: int8 for /recommendation-route" with expected cost delta and a small eval score delta if available.
[07:40] Priya: How do you validate the "eval score" delta? We need to ensure no regressions.
[07:49] Sofia: We tie this to Redwood Optimize evals. You can link a prompt set and we'll run the model variants and show delta in quality metrics. It's optional but useful.
[08:10] Maya: Security question - we need KMS + HSM support and audit logs for all inference requests.
[08:20] Ethan: For Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS, and all request metadata is logged to an append-only audit stream. We also support SSO/SAML and RBAC for console access.
[08:33] Oliver: Are logs stored in your cloud or do we push to our SIEM?
[08:40] Ethan: Both options. You can route logs to your CloudWatch/BigQuery/ELK; for Private we can also write to your internal storage.
[08:53] Priya: Does per-route cost allocation support multi-tenant labeling? We have multiple product teams hitting same endpoint.
[09:00] Sofia: Yes - there's a tagging system. You can add headers or auth-scopes; the console breaks down by tag and you can assign cost centers. There's also a chargeback CSV export.
[09:18] Maya: Good. Show the cost breakdown export.
[09:24] Sofia: Export example - columns: route, tag, model_variant, tokens_generated, compute_seconds, estimated_cost, region. You can pull this daily or on-demand.
[09:40] Oliver: Excellent. One more - how do fallbacks work? If primary model runs out of capacity, what's the console show?
[09:48] Sofia: We show auto-fallback events in the route timeline. Policy tells us whether to fallback to cheaper model or increase capacity. You can set canary policies and auto-fallback thresholds.
[10:10] Ethan: Real customer note - a retail client used fallbacks to avoid outages on Black Friday and the console helped them debug latency spikes quickly.
[10:25] Maya: Nice.
[10:30] Sofia: Quick demo of a sample cost drilldown - clicking a high-cost spike we see the actual requests, tokens per request, model used, batching window, and whether there was a cache miss.
[11:00] Sofia: You can replay request timeline (sanitized) and correlate with infra metrics: GPU utilization, network egress, and slot contention.
[11:20] Priya: For the POC we'll want the raw per-request CSV to reconcile with our internal billing.
[11:28] Sofia: We'll provide that.
[11:32] Maya: Let's talk SLA and Dedicated terms - we need 99.9% p99 latency under certain throughput.
[11:42] Ethan: Dedicated has SLA tiers and reserved pools; we can map throughput commitments into dedicated slots with predictable p99s. We'll include capacity planning in the pricing doc.
[12:00] Oliver: Pricing - give us ranges for Hosted vs Dedicated per million tokens and what committed discounts look like.
[12:10] Ethan: I'll send a pricing sheet after the call. Hosted pricing has usage tiers; Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commit. I'll include example cost per token including expected infra and support fees.
[12:28] Maya: Competitors - we compared to Anthropic and a couple of self-host options. How do you compare on observability?
[12:36] Sofia: We emphasize production telemetry - token-level, route-level cost allocation, and built-in eval hooks. Many do model outputs but not cost reconciliation and per-route chargeback out of the box.
[13:00] Priya: Ok that helps.
[13:05] Sofia: Last part - we'll walk through setting up the trial tenant. (walkthrough) You get a sample dashboard, pre-populated with sample traffic, and then you can upload a profile to match your real traffic.
[13:40] Sofia: Provisioning takes ~24 hours for Dedicated evals, hosted trial is immediate. For the benchmark POC we'll provision a trial and run a 1-week synthetic + replay of your traffic.
[14:00] Maya: Timeline - we want results before end of month, so a 1-week POC starting next week is ideal.
[14:08] Ethan: We can do that.
[14:12] Sofia: Any remaining questions?
[14:18] Oliver: One more technical - do you expose kernel-level timeline and NVLink metrics? Our infra team likes that granularity.
[14:28] Sofia: On Dedicated yes, we can surface NVLink and kernel timings; on Hosted we provide summarized telemetry but can provide deeper traces for benchmarking sessions.
[14:45] Priya: Ok good.
[14:50] Ethan: Quick recap and next steps - we'll: 1) send pricing deck and Dedicated vs Hosted attachment (Ethan), 2) Sofia will provision trial tenant and sample dashboards, 3) Maya will share traffic profiles and expected peaks, 4) schedule benchmarking POC next week.
[15:15] Maya: Sounds good - please include SOC2 and KMS docs in the packet.
[15:22] Ethan: Will do.
[15:25] (audio noise / cross talk)
[15:40] Sofia: I'll follow up in calendar with the POC invite and a checklist for what we need from your side.
[16:00] Maya: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[16:05] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.

(Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors present; product names sometimes referred to as "Redwood Dedicate" or "KV cash")

[42:00] End of recording

Meeting recap / action items listed above.
